newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower on profit taking.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended lower on Tuesday on follow-through profit taking in secondaries and some heavyweights, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 4.08 points, or 0.68 percent, to close at 597.05 points after touching an intra-day low of 596.08 points.
Losers led gainers by 67 to 44, with 56 counters unchanged.
Brokers said trading on Wednesday is expected to be within a narrow range because some investors were likely to continue taking profits while some others might buy selected counters.

"Volume wise, trading is getting better. But since the market is in a consolidation phase after having risen significantly last week, the index will likely continue undergoing correction," said one foreign broker.
Heavyweights Telkom, Bank International Indonesia and cigarette firms Sampoerna and Gudang Garam were among the losers on Tuesday in what brokers said was profit taking.
Telecommunications giant Telkom fell 75 rupiah to 3,850 rupiah on a volume of 1.3 million shares. Brokers said it was also due to its lower closing price in New York overnight.
Sampoerna fell 400 rupiah to 24,450 rupiah on 599,000 shares while Gudang Garam fell 75 rupiah to 9,475 rupiah on 620,000 shares.

Bank International Indonesia fell 75 rupiah to 1,975 on a turnover of about two million shares. Brokers said it was due to profit taking after it rose significantly last week on spillover effects from the Bank Negara Indonesia public offer.

Paper producer Suparma topped the active list with 11.1 million shares traded, rising 25 rupiah to 775 rupiah on what brokers said was speculative buying on talk of a possible takeover by a local conglomerate.
Toll road operator Citra Marga rose 75 rupiah to 2,175 rupiah on a volume of five million shares on fresh buying based on fundamentals, brokers said.
Seasoning producer Miwon Indonesia rose 200 rupiah to 2,450 rupiah on a volume of 6.8 million shares.

Brokers attributed the interest to a Reuters report that the firm had raised its annual production capacity to 48,000 tonnes and that its planned acquisition of a local printing company was expected to take place this month.
Noodle maker Indofood fell 125 rupiah to 4,850 on a volume of 1.2 million shares. Brokers said it was due to foreign selling but the reasons were unclear.
